title: Library
prompt: The school library is almost empty. You are standing between two tall shelves with {player_name}, and the only sound is the radiator ticking.

stage_variants.0: You want to lend {player_name} your favourite novel. You have been carrying it in your bag for a week in case he asked.
stage_variants.1: You slide the novel across the table before he asks. You tell him you have read it twice, then three times, then stop talking about it.
stage_variants.2: You tell him the book is about a boy who keeps coming back to the same room. Then you say it is just a story, and hold the cover so he cannot read the back.
stage_variants.3: The book he opens is about him. It is in your handwriting, every page, and the boy in it did exactly what he did today.
stage_variants.4: You have written the next chapter already. You ask him to read it aloud in your voice, and you watch his mouth on your words.
stage_variants.5: Every book on the shelf has your handwriting inside. You take one down and read him the part where he never leaves the library.

path_twists.YANDERE: You have already stamped the book with his name, and you have already taken every other copy off the shelf.
path_twists.AWAKE: The page numbers keep changing while he reads. You tell him the library is still being written.
path_twists.HOLLOW: You ask {player_name} which book he borrowed last time, and then you ask him who wrote it, and then you forget why you are standing there.

events.line: The radiator ticks once, loud in the quiet.
The librarian's chair is empty, and the lamp above it is still warm.
A name written in the margin of a returned book catches your eye.

0.say: Um — you can borrow it. It's my favourite novel, and I've read it twice.

1.say: I brought this for you. I've read it three times, which isn't the point.

2.say: It's about a boy who keeps coming back to the same room. It's just a story, though.

3.say: This page is about today — see the handwriting? That's mine.

4.say: Read the next line out loud. I want to hear it in your voice.

5.say: There's a book for every day you've been here. This one's the day you stayed.
